text:
Chinese Gang Uses Drones To Smuggle $80 Million Worth Of Smartphones By 0 
A Chinese gang is on the cutting edge of smuggling stolen goods by using drones to successfully transport close to $80 million worth of Apple ( AAPL ) iPhones and other smartphones. 
According to CNN , the suspects transported as many 15,000 devices every night, smuggling them from Hong Kong neighboring city of Shenzhen. Authorities have now detained the suspects. 
“Authorities said the gang used drones to suspend two, 200 meter-long cables between buildings on either side of the border,” reports CNN. “Bags carrying smartphones were attached to the cables and then pulled over to Shenzhen.” 
Chinese state media claims that customs officers were taken aback by the scenario, which is the first of its kind they’ve come across. More from CNN: 
China has stepped up efforts to regulate use of drones in the country. Last year, the government brought in rules including a requirement for drones over a certain weight to be registered under their owners’ real names , according to state media. 
The crackdown followed an incident where drones were flown illegally over an airport in southwestern China, causing chaos for local air traffic. 
Smuggling drones have become an increasing problem here in the United States at the southern border, where cartels have been caught using them to transport drugs into the country. 
Brandon Judd, an agent and president of the National Border Patrol Council, has even warned that Border Patrol agencies do not have the technology to combat the problem. “The number is just astronomical,” Judd told The Washington Times . 
Fox News notes that “defending against drones are inherently challenging and there are no policies in place, which is reportedly a source of frustration for patrol agents.” 
Rep. Vicky Hartzler (R-MO) introduced a bill last year that would allow border patrol agents more flexibility when dealing with drones.
